200.description:
One Harvard Gazette story by URL or slug, read from the Gazette's public WordPress REST API: headline, dek, byline and affiliation, publication and update times, section, categories, tags, featured image, the body as Markdown and its links. `max_chars` caps the body. Unknown stories are `not_found`.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `author` | string | Byline as printed (the post's author field), else the WordPress author name. |
| `author_affiliation` | string | Byline affiliation, e.g. Harvard Staff Writer. |
| `categories` | string[] | Every category the story is filed under. |
| `chars` | number | Length of the full body in characters before truncation. |
| `content` | string | Story body as Markdown (paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes, captions, links). The header block (headline, byline, hero image) is returned as fields instead. |
| `id` | number | WordPress post id. |
| `image_url` | string | Featured image URL. |
| `links` | object[] | Distinct links in the body, in order. |
| `modified_at` | string | Last modification time, UTC ISO 8601. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number | When the source was read (epoch ms). |
| `published_at` | string | Publication time, UTC ISO 8601. |
| `section` | string | Primary Gazette section, e.g. Health, Science & Tech. |
| `slug` | string |  |
| `subtitle` | string | Dek / excerpt shown under the headline. |
| `tags` | string[] | Topic tags. |
| `title` | string |  |
| `truncated` | boolean |  |
| `url` | string | Canonical story URL on news.harvard.edu. |

value.author: Sy Boles
value.content:
In the mid-1970s, Harvard curator Barbara “Bobbie” Norfleet crisscrossed America in a red sports car, hunting for photos for Harvard’s collections. She wasn’t interested in the classical fine-art photography that was then beginning to be curated by the big-name museums. She wanted images of everyday life — the wedding portraits, kids’ dance recitals, and other social rituals.

It was an era of change in the photography industry. More Americans owned their own cameras; more companies and government agencies had photographers on staff. The professional photography studio, which had been a mainstay of community life since the late 1800s, was dying out.

Over the course of two years, Norfleet met with photo studio heads, reviewed thousands upon thousands of negatives, and carted her finds — ultimately more than 20,000 images — back to Harvard in the trunk of her car (or in a suitcase on an airplane).

Now, half a century later, a selection of her finds is on display at the Harvard Art Muse
value.subtitle: Half a century after curator’s road trip collecting photos of American life, a look at what’s inside — and outside — the frames
value.title: Selective nostalgia

200.description:
Search Harvard Gazette stories by keyword with the Gazette's WordPress search, or list the latest stories when `q` is omitted. Returns id, slug, URL, title, excerpt, byline, publication time and section per story, with totals and `next_page` for paging. A query with no matches returns an empty list.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `next_page` | number | Pass as page for the next results; null on the last page. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number | When the source was read (epoch ms). |
| `page` | number |  |
| `query` | string | Normalized query; null lists the latest stories. |
| `results` | object[] | Stories, newest first for listings, by relevance for searches. |
| `total` | number | Total matching stories; null for a page past the end. |
| `total_pages` | number |  |
